about.title: About
about.firstParagraph: I'm a software engineer with about four years building web platforms end to end. I work at Gupy, Brazil's largest HR-tech, on the Admission product — shipping full-stack features in Node.js and React, both in TypeScript.
about.secondParagraph: I care about building maintainable and scalable code, made to last. I lean on domain-driven design, and I like bringing a critical eye to a project — weighing alternatives that come out leaner and more efficient than the obvious one.
about.thirdParagraph: Before Gupy I worked across the stack at MadeiraMadeira, one of Brazil's biggest online retailers, writing Go services that processed close to a million events a day and Python tooling that replaced manual spreadsheet work. I'm finishing a Computer Science degree at Feevale, and I build my own tools on the side — like Domainbook, a living-documentation system I use across projects such as Commander Playtester.

blurbs.commander: A browser tool that measures how strong a Magic: The Gathering Commander deck is — pilot or watch rules-accurate games against opponent decks (a Rust/WASM engine), or run a fast Monte-Carlo simulation for win rates.
blurbs.domainbook: Living documentation for codebases worked on by agents: git-versioned markdown, an explorable site, an MCP server, and a git hook that blocks changes without a matching doc update.
blurbs.timer: A Fallout Pip-Boy themed countdown timer with a built-in music player and a detonation sequence when it hits zero.

academic.title: Academic Experience
feevale: Feevale is a Brazilian university with 3 campuses and a Tech-Park hosting more than 100 companies. It offers over 100 undergraduate and postgraduate programs across many fields.

I am taking an undegraduate degree in Computer Science at the institution. I hope to acquire a deeper technical knowledge related to my daily tasks as a Developer. I am also looking forward to an increase in my low-level computational expertise so I can set myself apart from other professionals.
trybe: Trybe is a web development school that has a genuine commitment to the professional success of its students. With the Shared Success Model, those who study at Trybe have the option of paying only when they are already working.

There are more than 1500 hours of training that covers the fundamental of web development, development, Front-end, Back-end, computer science, software engineering, agile methodologies and soft skills.
I did the course to learn how to learn and to code. During the course, I acquired most of the technical knowledge I would need afterwards to work in the area.
ifsul: IFSul is a federal institute of education in Brazil, offering high-quality integrated technical courses alongside high school — among them Information Technology and Electronics.

There I graduated in high school along with the Information Technology Course. The Course went through a lot of content about Network, Programming, Operational Systems and Hardware Maintence. It added a lot to my academic experience and there I was inspired to do my first projects in the form of Mobile Apps with Bluetooth, Android Studio, Firebase and React Native integrations.
successEnglish: Success English is a well-regarded English-language school. It uses the Top Notch book series and its tests to take students from fundamentals to advanced English. The course relies on written and spoken tests to evaluate each student's performance.

The institution is recognized by their high-achieving students in the English Language, with a very effective method applied over the years. There I was able to learn most of what I currently know, and with the constant contact with the language I am able to keep a good English level overall.

professional.title: Professional Experience
gupy: Gupy is Brazil's largest HR-tech, leading the market in recruiting and HR software. I work on the Admission product — the flow that turns a hire into an onboarded employee.

I ship full-stack features here, mostly Node.js services and React front-ends, both in TypeScript. I reworked an internal validation step that was holding candidates and the team up, cutting the wait on both sides. I lean on domain-driven design with unit and integration tests to keep the product maintainable as it grows.
madeiraMadeira: MadeiraMadeira is one of Brazil's biggest online retailers and one of the country's unicorns. I worked on the back-office and on processes tied to carriers and shipping.

On the back end I wrote Go services that processed close to a million events a day, powering internal charging that prevented revenue leakage, plus Python tooling that replaced manual spreadsheet work. On the front end I built with React, NX, Jest and Cypress.
renovareTelecom: Renovare Telecom is a telecommunications company. I joined as an IT Technician, responsible for installing and maintaining the company's computers.

I set up an internal ticketing system that streamlined the support workflow, and handled cloning and restoring operating systems across the fleet. It's where I got comfortable with enterprise servers and day-to-day Linux.
kundenSystems: Kunden Systems is an ERP provider serving clients across South America. It was my first professional experience in IT.

I installed and maintained computers, managed local and remote servers, and applied fixes to PL/SQL test and production databases. It's where I learned the fundamentals from colleagues with years in the field.

welcome.title: Welcome to my Portfolio!
welcome.intro: You've booted into my portfolio — built as a small synthwave operating system. It's made to be explored: launch the apps in the dock, dig through the files, run my projects in the Browser, or poke around the Terminal.
welcome.meIntro: Behind all of it: I'm Rafael, a software engineer who builds web platforms end to end. Most of my time goes to backend and full-stack work — Node.js, Go and TypeScript. That said, as you can see some of my time is also spent with some unusual stuff like this project =D
